claim.quote: central Au+Au collisions at RHIC produce dense, rapidly thermalizing matter characterized by: (1) initial energy densities above the critical values predicted by lattice QCD for establishment of a Quark-Gluon Plasma (QGP); (2) nearly ideal fluid flow

key_value_text.quote: the measurements themselves do not yet establish unequivocal evidence for a transition to this new form of matter
key_value_text.value: Dense, rapidly thermalizing matter with initial energy densities above the lattice-QCD critical value and nearly-ideal (near-zero viscosity) fluid flow; the collaboration states its own measurements 'do not yet establish unequivocal evidence for a transition to this new form of matter.'

name: Experimental and Theoretical Challenges in the Search for the Quark Gluon Plasma: The STAR Collaboration's Critical Assessment of the Evidence from RHIC Collisions
notes: Historically significant STAR 'white paper' from RHIC's widely publicised 2005 announcements. Per the wave-3 brief, this is recorded with the collaboration's own title wording and result_type 'measurement' (never 'discovery'); the collaboration's own abstract explicitly hedges on 'evidence'.

significance.locator: arXiv:nucl-ex/0501009, abstract (no single significance/sigma value stated)
significance.note: This is a collaboration-wide assessment paper covering many measurements, not a single-significance result; the collaboration's own abstract explicitly states the measurements 'do not yet establish unequivocal evidence for a transition to this new form of matter' -- recorded as a measurement, never as a discovery or observation, per the brief's explicit instruction.

summary.plain: In 2005, the STAR collaboration published its own critical assessment of four years of RHIC gold-ion collision data, describing a dense, rapidly-flowing form of matter unlike anything seen before, while being careful to say the evidence for a genuine new phase of matter was not yet conclusive.
summary.technical: STAR's 2005 white paper (Nucl. Phys. A 757, 102-183) reviews RHIC Run-1 through Run-4 Au+Au data: initial energy densities exceeding the lattice-QCD QGP threshold and near-ideal-fluid elliptic flow, while explicitly stating the data do not yet unequivocally establish a phase transition.

title: Experimental and Theoretical Challenges in the Search for the Quark Gluon Plasma: The STAR Collaboration's Critical Assessment of the Evidence from RHIC Collisions
why_it_matters: One of the four RHIC collaborations' widely reported 2005 assessments that framed RHIC collisions as producing a strongly-coupled, nearly-perfect liquid rather than a weakly-interacting parton gas, reshaping the theoretical picture of the quark-gluon plasma.
